structure: Part 4, organisation scoping and caller identity. Read in full: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/filter/IdentityHeaderFilter.java (180 lines: the one identity header, its presence and format checks, the /organisation/ path test that decides which requests are checked, the path-orgId versus header comparison, the self-written problem+json rejections, the logging context and the trust-boundary Javadoc); src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/address/OperatorController.java (368 lines, read for the class-level scoping, the authoriseOrg guard and the identity-header parameter on all five operations; per-endpoint behaviour left to parts 2 and 3); README.md section 'Security and trust boundary' (lines 83-109, plus the scoping sentence at the head of 'API overview', lines 113-115); src/test/java/.../filter/IdentityHeaderFilterTest.java (12 unit tests); src/test/java/.../integration/AddressScopingIT.java (7 integration tests). Covered: the single identity header the service reads (Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id) and every rejection when it is missing, blank or malformed; the exemption of every path outside /organisation/; the 404 for a path orgId that disagrees with the header, at both the filter and the controller guard; that the stored and queried organisation always comes from the header; cross-organisation isolation for list, read, create, update and delete; the no-existence-disclosure rule for 404s; the trust boundary in general terms; and what each of the 19 tests proves. Gaps recorded where the slice is silent: no user-level identity, no proof that a filter-level mismatch 404 matches an unknown-id 404 byte for byte, and no in-service enforcement of the upstream boundary.

claims.statement: The service identifies the calling organisation from one HTTP request header, Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id.
Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id is the only tenant key for organisation-scoped reads and writes.
claims.quote: {@code Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id} is the sole tenant key for org-scoped reads and writes.

claims.statement: The service reads no user-level identity (no user id, email or role header): scoping is by organisation only, so every caller from the same organisation sees and changes the same address book.
claims.note: Inferred from a grep of src/main for getHeader and @RequestHeader: the only identity header read is the organisation header (RequestTracingFilter reads a trace header, which is not identity and belongs to another part).

claims.statement: The identity check applies to every request whose path starts with /organisation/.
Every path outside /organisation/, such as the /health check, is exempt from the identity check and passes through without the header.
A request to an /organisation/ path with no Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header is rejected with HTTP 400 before any handler runs.
claims.quote: reject(response, HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, BAD_REQUEST_TYPE, "Bad Request", "Missing required header " + ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER);

claims.statement: A Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header that is present but blank or only whitespace is treated as missing and rejected with HTTP 400.
The missing-or-blank header rejection reads: title "Bad Request", detail "Missing required header Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request.
An organisation id is well formed only when it is 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, underscore or hyphen.
A Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header that is present but not well formed (for example, containing spaces) is rejected with HTTP 400.
The malformed-header rejection reads: title "Bad Request", detail "Invalid Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request.
An identity-header rejection is an RFC 9457 problem with content type application/problem+json, carrying type, title, status and detail.
claims.quote: Problem problem = new Problem(type, title, status.value(), detail, traceId);

claims.statement: An identity-header 400 carries no errors map: it is a platform rejection of the caller, not a field validation error a form could show against a field.
claims.quote:
a missing or blank identity header is a platform auth rejection — a 400 bad-request problem
 *       with NO {@code errors} map — not a body-field business validation error.

claims.statement: A missing identity header is a 400, never a 401 or 403.
An identity-header rejection carries the request's trace id as traceId when one is present, and omits the field when there is none.
Every address operation lives under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses, so every operation is scoped by the organisation in its path.
The path orgId is never trusted on its own: every operation authorises it against the caller's Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header.
A request whose path orgId differs from the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header is rejected with HTTP 404 by the identity filter, before any handler or store lookup runs.
The path-versus-header comparison is an exact, case-sensitive match.
claims.note: Inferred from String.equals: no test exercises a case-only difference.

claims.statement: The path-mismatch rejection reads: title "Resource Not Found", detail "Address not found", type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/not-found.
A caller from another organisation always gets 404, never 403, so the API never discloses that another organisation's addresses exist.
claims.quote:
A
   * mismatch throws {@link NotFoundException} → 404 (never 403): the API must not disclose that
   * another organisation's addresses exist (cv-040).

claims.statement: Each operation also checks the path orgId against the header inside the controller and answers a mismatch with 404 "Address not found", a second guard behind the filter.
claims.quote:
if (!sessionOrg.equals(orgId)) {
      throw new NotFoundException("Address not found");
claims.note: Because the filter rejects a mismatch first, this guard is not reached on a normal request; it is defence in depth.

claims.statement: The identity header is required on every operation: list, create, fetch, replace and soft delete.
Every operation reads and writes the store under the organisation from the identity header, not the path or body.
A created address's organisationId is stamped from the identity header, never taken from the request body.
claims.quote:
{@code organisationId} is stamped from the
   * identity header, never from the body;

claims.statement: An address id belonging to another organisation, used under the caller's own organisation path, is a 404 on fetch, replace and delete, because the organisation scope is applied in the store query.
claims.quote:
the scope is enforced in the query, so a cross-org id is a 404 byte-for-byte identical to an
 *       unknown id (no existence and no deletion leak);

claims.statement: A 404 for another organisation's address is byte-for-byte identical to a 404 for an id that does not exist, and carries no instance field.
claims.quote: // Identical problem — a 404 carries no existence and no deletion information.

claims.statement: No test proves that the filter's path-mismatch 404 is identical to the 404 for an unknown id; the filter writes its own problem body while an in-scope miss goes through the shared exception handler.
claims.note: Looked in IdentityHeaderFilterTest (checks only status and type for the mismatch) and AddressScopingIT (compares only an in-scope cross-org id with an unknown id).

claims.statement: The service has no authentication layer of its own: it does not validate JWTs or API keys, and treats the organisation header as already authenticated.
claims.ref: README.md: Security and trust boundary (line 85); IdentityHeaderFilter.java:33-35
claims.quote: This service has **no Spring Security layer** and does not validate JWTs or API keys.

claims.statement: Separating one organisation's addresses from another's relies entirely on a trusted forwarded-header contract with the hop in front of the service.
claims.quote:
Tenant
isolation relies entirely on a trusted-forwarded-header contract:

claims.statement: Authenticating the caller through Defra ID (OIDC) is the job of the CDP ingress or the calling frontend (for example ins-frontend), not this service.
claims.ref: README.md: Security and trust boundary, responsibility table row 1
claims.quote: | Authenticate the caller (Defra ID / OIDC) | CDP ingress or calling BFF (e.g. ins-frontend) |

claims.statement: The upstream hop must discard any organisation header the end user's client sends and set it from the verified session's organisation.
claims.ref: README.md: Security and trust boundary, responsibility table rows 2-3
claims.quote: | Set `Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id` from the verified session | Same upstream hop |

claims.statement: CDP network policy must stop callers reaching the service without going through the authenticated upstream hop.
claims.ref: README.md: Security and trust boundary, responsibility table row 4 and line 105
claims.quote: **Production requirement:** callers must not reach this service without the upstream hop above.

claims.statement: The organisation boundary depends on deployment controls outside the service; the service cannot enforce it alone if those controls are absent, and adding its own resource-server authentication was deferred.
claims.quote:
the service cannot defend itself against a trusted-network
violation without adding a resource server (deferred for this ticket).
claims.note: Security finding stated in general terms only, per the repo brief.

claims.statement: Nothing in the repo proves the upstream boundary is in place: no test or config here shows header stripping or network policy, which the README places with other owners.
claims.ref: README.md: Security and trust boundary; src/test (IdentityHeaderFilterTest, AddressScopingIT)
claims.note: Looked in the part's tests and README; the upstream hop and network policy are owned elsewhere (ins-frontend, CDP).

claims.statement: While a request is processed, the caller's organisation id is added to the logging context as organisationId, and removed afterwards even if the request fails.
Each identity rejection is logged as a warning naming the reason and the trace id, with no address personal data.
The identity filter runs near the very start of request handling, ahead of the application's own handlers.
The published API contract declares Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id as the security requirement for every address operation.
The published API contract documents a 400 for a missing header and a 404 for a path orgId that does not match the caller's organisation header on the address operations.
claims.quote: description = "Path orgId does not match the caller's organisation header",
claims.note: Fetch, replace and delete describe their 404 as 'Unknown id, or an id outside the caller's organisation scope'; fetch documents no 400 response at all, though the filter returns one.

claims.statement: Test: a request with no organisation header gets a 400 bad-request problem with application/problem+json, a detail naming the header and no errors map, and is not passed on.
Test: the missing-header rejection works whether the path arrives as the servlet path or only as the request URI.
Test: a whitespace-only organisation header gets a 400 bad-request problem with no errors map.
Test: GET, POST, PUT and DELETE without the organisation header are each stopped with a 400 naming the header.
claims.quote: .as("chain must halt for %s without the org-id header", method)

claims.statement: Test: a valid header matching the path lets the request through, with the organisation id in the logging context.
Test: the 400 body carries the trace id of the request.
Test: /health is not checked for the identity header and gets no rejection body.
Test: a header of org-b on an org-a path is stopped with a 404 not-found problem before the request is passed on.
Test: the organisation id is cleared from the logging context after a successful request.
Test: the organisation id is cleared from the logging context when request handling throws.
Test: an organisation header containing spaces is rejected with 400.
Test: rejection logging contains no address personal data such as a business name or email.
Test: organisation B listing its own book does not see organisation A's address, gets 404 fetching, replacing or deleting A's id under its own path, and A's address stays live.
claims.quote: // org B gets 404 on GET / PUT / DELETE of A's id under B's own scope

claims.statement: Test: a caller whose header is organisation B is refused with 404 on list, fetch, replace, delete and create against organisation A's path; A's address stays ACTIVE and no new address is saved for A.
claims.quote: // a create against another org's path is rejected and persists nothing new

claims.statement: Test: listing with no organisation header is a 400 application/problem+json bad-request with no errors map.
Test: listing with a blank organisation header is a 400 application/problem+json bad-request with no errors map.
Test: creating an address with no organisation header is a 400 with no errors map, and nothing is saved.
Test: a created address is stored and returned with the caller's organisationId, and appears in that organisation's list.
claims.quote: // organisationId is stamped from the trusted identity, never the body (cv-010)

claims.statement: Test: organisation B's 404 for organisation A's live address equals its 404 for an unknown id, and neither has an instance field.
The scoping rules trace to two earlier rulings, cv-010 (the trusted forwarded-header identity contract) and cv-040 (authorise the session organisation against the path, 404 never 403).
claims.quote: forwarded header (cv-010, cv-040): the path is never trusted alone.
claims.note: The ruling ids are cited in code comments; the ruling texts themselves are not in this part's files.
